sections.title: What Neon is
sections.intent: Say what the app is, why it exists, and how it is built.

lines.say: This is Neon Video Studio. It's a desktop video editor I built, and every button in it is also a command, so an agent can edit a video while I watch.
lines.show: Title card.

props.title: Neon Video Studio
props.subtitle: A video editor you can drive by hand or by agent

lines.say: I wanted one tool for cutting videos without bouncing between apps, and one that an agent could run from start to finish.
lines.show: The same title card holds.

props.title: Neon Video Studio
props.subtitle: A video editor you can drive by hand or by agent

lines.say: Under the hood, a Bun process owns the project. The window is React. Frames come from Neon's own engine, and Yjs keeps every copy of the project in sync.
lines.show: Architecture: Bun main process in the middle, React window, motion engine, Yjs and the CLI around it.

props.title: One project, many hands
props.items:
Bun main process: owns the project, serves the API
React window: timeline, preview, panels
@neon/motion: frames for preview and export
Yjs: every copy stays in sync
neon-cli: the same API from a terminal

sections.title: Projects
sections.intent: The projects overview: recent projects, new project, folders.

lines.say: Projects open from this overview. Each project is a folder with its media inside, so I can copy it to another machine and open it there.
lines.show: Start page with four recent projects.

lines.say: A new project takes a name, a format and a frame rate. Vertical and square formats are there for shorts.
lines.show: Type a name, open the format list.

lines.say: I'll open the launch trailer for my Git client.
lines.show: Click Git Gud launch trailer; the editor opens.

sections.title: Editing the timeline
sections.intent: Tracks, drag, trim, snap, split, placing media, undo, shortcuts.

lines.say: The timeline has video, audio and FX tracks. Clips draw their waveform, so I can see where someone is talking.
lines.show: Sweep over the tracks and the waveforms.

lines.say: Drag a clip to move it. It snaps to the playhead and to the edges of other clips.
lines.show: Drag the last clip away and back until it snaps.

lines.say: Drag an edge to trim. Trimming the start slides into the footage.
lines.show: Trim the start of the third clip.

lines.say: The S key splits whatever sits under the playhead.
lines.show: Move the playhead, press S.

lines.say: Add at playhead puts media in the first free spot on the track, so it never lands on top of another clip.
lines.show: Media panel, add at playhead; the shot lands after the last clip.

lines.say: Undo takes back only my own edits. That matters once an agent or another person is editing the same project.
lines.show: Undo twice.

lines.say: The question mark key lists every shortcut.
lines.show: Shortcuts dialog.

sections.title: Templates and the inspector
sections.intent: Templates are React clips; inspector is schema driven; canvas editing; animations.

lines.say: Titles, lower thirds and captions are React components. They sit on FX tracks like any other clip.
lines.show: FX panel with live previews.

lines.say: Each card in the FX panel is a live preview. Click one and it lands at the playhead.
lines.show: Click Lower Third.

lines.say: The inspector builds its fields from the component's schema. I change the text and the preview follows.
lines.show: Type a new title in the inspector.

lines.say: I can drag it on the canvas too. It snaps to the centre and the thirds.
lines.show: Drag the lower third on the preview.

lines.say: Every element can animate in and out with a fade, a slide or a pop.
lines.show: Set the in animation to pop and play.

sections.title: FX packs
sections.intent: What a pack is, installing one, using its components.

lines.say: When the built-in set isn't enough, I write an FX pack. It's a folder with a pack.json that describes every field, and an index.tsx with the components.
lines.show: Card: the files of a pack.

props.title: A pack is a folder

lines.say: The Library lists the packs on this machine. Install folder adds one, and so does neon-cli packs install, which I'm running here.
lines.show: FX Library; the Neon Tour pack appears as the CLI installs it.

lines.say: Its components show up straight away, with previews. The titles and diagrams in this video come from this pack, in Neon's colours.
lines.show: Components list filtered to the Neon Tour pack; add Neon title.

lines.say: A project keeps a copy of every pack it uses, so it still renders on a machine that never installed them.
lines.show: The Soft Title clip playing.

sections.title: Script and prompter
sections.intent: Script view, statuses, notes, prompter that re-records one line.

lines.say: My videos start as a script. The Script view holds sections of lines, each with what I say and what the picture shows.
lines.show: Script view of the trailer.

lines.say: A section is a draft, waiting on me, or approved. Notes pin to a line, and an agent reads and answers them from the CLI.
lines.show: Notes margin; an agent reply appears.

lines.say: In the editor, the prompter shows the line under the playhead.
lines.show: Prompter panel follows the playhead.

lines.say: Record line counts me in, plays that stretch of the timeline and records just that line. The new take replaces the old one only once it has saved.
lines.show: Hover Re-record line.

sections.title: Screen demos and AI
sections.intent: Recording, local AI engines, silence trimming, enhance, zooms.

lines.say: For screen demos, the screen button records the display and my microphone into one file. This machine hasn't granted screen recording, so here I'm using a recording I already have.
lines.show: Hover the screen button; a narrated recording sits on V1.

lines.say: The AI panel runs local engines. The pills show what this machine has: ffmpeg, Apple Vision and yt-dlp are ready, and speech recognition isn't installed.
lines.show: AI panel engine pills.

lines.say: Silence trimming needs no model. It finds the pauses and shortens each one, and the cuts land as normal edits I can undo.
lines.show: Run Trim silences; the clip splits and closes up.

lines.say: Enhance gives a clearer voice at broadcast loudness. It writes a new file and keeps the original in the media library.
lines.show: Run Enhance; job progress, new asset.

lines.say: With whisper.cpp installed, the same panel cuts the ums, and the transcript becomes an editor: select words, press delete, and they're gone from the video.
lines.show: The install box for speech recognition.

lines.say: A zoom eases in on the part that matters, and it stays on that moment through later cuts.
lines.show: Add a zoom from the inspector and play through it.

sections.title: Thumbnails
sections.intent: Thumb tab: timeline frame background, layers from packs.

lines.say: The Thumb tab builds the YouTube thumbnail from the same components. The background is a frame of the timeline.
lines.show: Thumb tab, background at playhead.

lines.say: Layers stack on top, and this title comes from my pack. The CLI builds the same thumbnail, which is how this video got its own.
lines.show: Add the Neon thumbnail layer; the layer list.

sections.title: Render and publish
sections.intent: Render panel, presets, a running render, YouTube publishing.

lines.say: Render exports an H.264 MP4 through the same engine as the preview. Presets run from a quick draft up to 4K, vertical and square.
lines.show: Render panel, preset list.

lines.say: The render runs in a separate worker, so I can keep editing while it goes.
lines.show: Start a draft render; progress bar.

lines.say: Once I sign in with Google, the same panel uploads to YouTube with the title, description, tags, visibility, a schedule and the project thumbnail.
lines.show: YouTube upload form.

sections.title: Driving it from the CLI
sections.intent: neon-cli side by side with the app; Live panel; plans; stills.

lines.say: Everything so far is also a command. neon-cli talks to the running app over a local API, and every change it makes shows up live in the window.
lines.show: Diagram: agent, neon-cli, control API, app window.

props.title: Same edits, from a terminal
props.items:
Agent: plans the edit
neon-cli: commands and plans
Control API: local port and token
Neon window: changes appear live

lines.say: Here's a terminal next to the app. neon-cli timeline prints the edit as text, with the id of every clip.
lines.show: Terminal: neon-cli timeline.

lines.say: The agent inserts a lower third. It lands on the timeline, and the Live panel logs it as a CLI edit.
lines.show: Terminal insert; the clip flashes; Live panel entry.

lines.say: Bigger changes go in a plan file. Apply runs every step as one undo step, or rolls the lot back if one fails.
lines.show: Terminal apply plan.json; several clips appear.

lines.say: And the still command renders a frame to a PNG, so the agent can look at its own work before it renders.
lines.show: Terminal still; the PNG path prints.

sections.title: Editing together
sections.intent: Rooms: host, join, live edits both ways, peer playheads.

lines.say: Rooms put two people on one project. One machine hosts, and the other joins with the room code. There's no server in the middle.
lines.show: Two windows; the second joins the first's room.

lines.say: Edits from either side show up on both, and each person can see where the other one's playhead is.
lines.show: Edit on the left, it appears on the right; peer playhead.
